<section class="reader-section cool" id="the-problem" aria-label="The problem" data-step>
<span class="testpoint" data-testpoint aria-hidden="true">01</span>

<p class="kicker">The problem</p>

## Every file your AI reads uses up your plan

Tools like Claude Code and Codex can read your code, plan a change, and make it. But every file they read and every step they take counts against your plan's usage limit. Much of that work is routine: reading files, searching, and summarizing. When the limit runs out, you wait.

<div class="idea-card">
<p class="kicker">The idea</p>
<h3>Let a local helper do the reading</h3>
<figure class="delegation" role="img" aria-label="Diagram: the paid model, Claude Code or Codex, sends routine reading and coding to a local helper, Qwen3.8 on your computer. The helper sends checked work back.">
  <div class="delegation-grid" aria-hidden="true">
    <div class="chip"><p class="chip-tag"><span class="chip-dot paid"></span>U1 · PAID</p><p class="chip-name">Paid model</p><p class="chip-sub">Claude Code / Codex</p></div>
    <div class="wires-v">
      <div class="wire-v"><div class="sig-wire sig-wire-down" style="--pulse: #dc143c"></div><p>routine reading and coding</p></div>
      <div class="wire-v"><div class="sig-wire sig-wire-up" style="--pulse: #3c89c6"></div><p>checked work</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="wires-h">
      <div class="wire-h"><p>routine reading and coding</p><div class="sig-hwire sig-hwire-right" style="--pulse: #dc143c"></div></div>
      <div class="wire-h"><p>checked work</p><div class="sig-hwire sig-hwire-left" style="--pulse: #3c89c6"></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chip"><p class="chip-tag"><span class="chip-dot local"></span>U2 · LOCAL</p><p class="chip-name">Local helper</p><p class="chip-sub">Qwen3.8 · runs locally</p></div>
  </div>
</figure>
<p>Researchers at Stanford tested this idea in a 2025 study called MinionS. A small model on a laptop read long documents while a cloud model, GPT-4o, directed the work. The cloud bill fell about 5.7 times, and the answers kept 97.9% of the cloud model's accuracy.</p>
<p class="study-caveat">That study asked questions about long documents: company financial reports, patient records, and science papers. It did not test coding, and it did not test Qwen3.8. So we need our own evidence.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15964">Read the MinionS study (Stanford, 2025)</a></p>
</div>

</section>

<section class="reader-section warm" id="the-test" aria-label="The test" data-step>
<span class="testpoint" data-testpoint aria-hidden="true">02</span>

<p class="kicker">Step one</p>

## Is the helper good enough?

Before a helper can take work off your plan, it has to do the work well. So we started there. We tested Qwen3.8, an open AI model anyone can download, running entirely on a Mac with 128 GB of memory. Nothing was sent to the cloud.

Four groups make this setup work:

<ol class="relationship-flow">
  <li><span>The model</span><strong>Qwen3.8-27B</strong><p>Built by the <a href="https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.8">Qwen Team</a>. An open model with 27 billion parameters, the values it learned in training.</p></li>
  <li><span>The engine</span><strong>Inco AI · Splash</strong><p><a href="https://inco.ai/blog/splash/">Inco AI</a> builds Splash, open-source software that runs the model fast on your own computer. It uses a compressed (4-bit) copy of the model plus a small DFlash 2 draft model that speeds up writing.</p></li>
  <li><span>The app</span><strong>LM Studio</strong><p>LM Studio loads Splash and the model and lets other programs send it requests.</p></li>
  <li><span>The tester</span><strong>Racecraft Lab</strong><p>Racecraft Lab, the technical innovation lab of Racecraft Systems, ran the tests and published the reviewed results.</p></li>
</ol>

We gave it two standard tests, called benchmarks. One checks real coding work. The other checks careful reasoning on hard science questions.

</section>

<section class="reader-section warm" id="what-it-means" aria-label="What it means" data-step>
<span class="testpoint" data-testpoint aria-hidden="true">04</span>

<p class="kicker">What it means</p>

## Promising enough to put to work

Running locally, Qwen3.8 did well enough to try as a helper for reading and everyday coding. It is not a replacement for the best cloud models on the hardest problems. And we have not yet measured the part that matters most: does handing it work actually save plan usage?

<div class="next-card">
<p class="kicker">What's next</p>
<p>We are building a delegation plugin for Claude Code and Codex, and we plan to open-source it. Early experiments are under way. Next, we will test the Unsloth build of Qwen3.8 and low-cost models on Ollama Cloud, then measure real savings. This site is the first chapter of that work.</p>
</div>

<section class="reader-section cool" aria-label="Key terms" data-step>
<span class="testpoint" data-testpoint aria-hidden="true">05</span>

## Key terms

<dl class="project-definitions" id="key-terms">
<div><dt>Local model</dt><dd>An AI model that runs on your own computer instead of a company's servers.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Delegation</dt><dd>Handing routine work from a paid AI tool to a cheaper helper, then checking what comes back.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Token</dt><dd>A small piece of text, often part of a word. AI plans and speeds are counted in tokens.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Benchmark</dt><dd>A standard test with known answers, used to measure AI systems the same way each time.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Splash / Qwen3.8</dt><dd>Short for the Qwen3.8-27B model running on Inco AI's Splash engine in LM Studio. Our results apply to this exact setup, not to every Qwen model or setting.</dd></div>
<div><dt>GPQA Diamond</dt><dd>198 hard multiple-choice questions in biology, chemistry, and physics, written by experts to be hard to look up.</dd></div>
<div><dt>SWE-bench Verified</dt><dd>500 real bugs from open-source projects. The AI must change the code so the project's own tests pass. The local result is 360 of 500 fixed.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Directional context</dt><dd>A published score from a different setup. Useful to show scale, not to rank models against each other.</dd></div>
</dl>
